claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself.
A Pulumi component state migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
The legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component's first version in the example creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC would require replacing the security group that refers to the VPC's ID, per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation.
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The example does not create a database.
The third version of the example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

In the AWSX VPC example, the Pulumi resource tree for v1 contains awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with Subnet and InternetGateway component children; v2 uses awsx:ec2:Vpc with managed aws resources beneath the VPC; v3 has plain aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as root.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and the components that group them; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, and modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot by themselves remove component wrappers and transfer references.
A Pulumi component registers a migration callback through the `stateMigrations` resource option, alongside an alias for the legacy component type.
The alias lets Pulumi find the old component; the migration callback receives the component's saved state followed by the state of its children.

The state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place, with the VPC keeping its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, and a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration.
Once both migrations have run, both callbacks return no result on later updates.

After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Before each upgrade in the example, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.

When users upgrade a component that ships a state migration and run Pulumi, Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update, without users writing the migration, attaching the callback, or editing stack state.
The VPC example repository contains all three programs and the migration code.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
Each successor mapping returned by a component state migration callback connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The state entries passed to a component state migration callback use the Pulumi checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
The Pulumi option reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a callback-api section explaining the callback API.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of component state migrations do not require removing an already-applied migration when using update plans or targeted updates.
